theorem_title: Section 5 — ordinary unboundedness of the compact coset family
formal_statement:
theorem ModNullUniversality.compact_coset_unboundedness :
    ∃ K : ModNullUniversality.CompactMetrizableHaarGroup,
      ModNullUniversality.IsAbelian K ∧
      ∃ H : ModNullUniversality.WF → Subgroup K.Carrier,
        ModNullUniversality.LowComplexityFamily K H ∧
        ∀ F : ModNullUniversality.StandardBorelEquivalence,
          ∃ T : ModNullUniversality.WF,
            ¬ ModNullUniversality.BorelReducible
              (ModNullUniversality.CosetRelation K (H T)) F.rel := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
There are one compact metrizable abelian group $K$, its normalized Haar probability, and a family $(H_T)_{T\in\mathrm{WF}}$ of subgroups of $K$ such that every subgroup and coset graph is $\Delta^0_3$, every graph is a difference of two $F_\sigma$ sets, and

$$\forall F\ \exists T\in\mathrm{WF}\quad E_{H_T}^K\not\leq_B F,$$

where $F$ ranges over all Borel equivalence relations on standard Borel spaces. The group and entire family are fixed before the target. This is the existential form of the compact-family conclusion established in the manuscript's unnumbered Section 5 argument. It concerns the whole group, without discarding a null set.
source: Universality modulo null sets in the Borel hierarchy, user-supplied unpublished manuscript dated 9 November 2026; SHA-256 48745c75427f83370292c2e4cf91ec06377e80472252db0182599edcd05e2d97, Section 5, unnumbered compact-family unboundedness argument, lines 361–395; its prior tensor-family input is Wang, arXiv:2611.02531v1, Corollary 6.1 and its proof. https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02531v1

readback.readback: Read-back author: Codex; the exact runtime model ID is unavailable. There exist a type $K$ in Lean's base type universe, a group structure on $K$, a compact metrizable topology on $K$ for which multiplication and inversion are continuous, a measurable-space structure on $K$ equal to the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of that topology, and a measure $\mu$ on this measurable space such that $\mu(K)=1$, every compact subset has measure strictly less than $\infty$, the pushforward of $\mu$ by $x\mapsto gx$ equals $\mu$ for every $g\in K$, and every nonempty open set has nonzero measure; moreover, $xy=yx$ for every $x,y\in K$. For this single choice of all these data there exists a function $T\mapsto H_T$ assigning a subgroup of $K$ to every index $T$ in the following set $\mathcal W$: an index is a Boolean-valued function $t$ on finite lists of natural numbers, together with the property that $t(s^\frown[n])=\mathrm{true}$ implies $t(s)=\mathrm{true}$ for every finite list $s$ and every $n\in\mathbb N$, and the property that there is no function $b:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ for which $t([b(0),\ldots,b(k-1)])=\mathrm{true}$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$. Here $\mathbb N$ contains $0$, the list at $k=0$ is the empty list, and both the empty tree (the constantly false predicate) and the tree consisting only of the empty list are among the indices. For every $T\in\mathcal W$, define $R_T=\{(x,y)\in K\times K:x^{-1}y\in H_T\}$, using the product topology on $K\times K$; both $H_T$ as a subset of $K$ and $R_T$ as a subset of $K\times K$ are simultaneously a union indexed by $\mathbb N$ of $G_\delta$ sets and an intersection indexed by $\mathbb N$ of $F_\sigma$ sets, where a $G_\delta$ set is an intersection of a countable family of open sets (the family may be empty, with intersection the entire ambient space) and an $F_\sigma$ set is a union indexed by $\mathbb N$ of closed sets. In addition, for every $T\in\mathcal W$ there are $F_\sigma$ subsets $A_T,B_T\subseteq K\times K$ such that $R_T=A_T\setminus B_T$; no inclusion between $A_T$ and $B_T$ is stipulated, and these witnesses and all preceding complexity witnesses may depend on $T$ and on the set being represented. There is no requirement that the assignment $T\mapsto H_T$ be measurable or that different indices have different subgroups. Finally, for every type $Y$ in Lean's base type universe equipped with a measurable-space structure admitting some compatible Polish topology (a second-countable topology induced by a complete metric whose Borel $\sigma$-algebra is the given measurable structure), and every relation $F$ on $Y$ that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive and whose graph $\{(u,v)\in Y\times Y:F(u,v)\}$ is measurable for the product measurable structure, there exists an index $T\in\mathcal W$ such that there is no function $f:K\to Y$ which is measurable for the specified measurable structures and satisfies $x^{-1}y\in H_T\iff F(f(x),f(y))$ for every $x,y\in K$. The index $T$ may depend on this target space and relation, while $K$, its structures and measure, and the whole family $(H_T)_{T\in\mathcal W}$ are chosen before the target; the equivalence condition concerns every pair of points, with no almost-everywhere qualification. The quantification over target spaces includes the empty space, for which the nonexistence of a function from the nonempty group $K$ already gives this no-reduction conclusion; all countable unions and intersections indexed by $\mathbb N$ include the index $0$ and may use repeated or empty constituent sets whenever the stated open or closed conditions allow them.
